name: a shallow rain puddle lying on the ground, reflecting a pale sky band, with a soft damp earth halo and only a faint low bank shadow along its far edge
label: wasteland_ruins/puddle

refSet.reason: 칩셋 wasteland_ruins 의 화풍 기준 묶음이 없다

surfaces.part: rain puddle (teal water with pale sky reflection)
damp earth halo and ground tile

answer.evidence: The 64x48 tile is a speckled brown dirt ground. The puddle is a small teal ellipse-like blob at about rows 20-28, roughly 13 px wide. Its width grows from a narrow top (rows 20-21) to a widest middle (rows 23-26) and narrows again to a point at row 28. It has a dark blue-teal far bank shadow along rows 20-22, and pale blue reflection streaks at rows 24-26. It has no front face, vertical wall or legs; it lies flat on the ground and is seen from above, as a flat decal should be. So there is no front face (0 rows).

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a brown soil field with sparse speckle and one small blue puddle in the middle. The measured facts are acceptable: 5 visible tones per tile against 3 for grass and 7 for paving, 1% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels. The puddle rim and soil specks lean brown, so the outline reads as a material tone, not a black sticker line. By eye, though, the puddle is tiny, only about 3 tones (rim, water, a light fleck), and it has no pale sky band. The damp-earth halo and the faint far-bank shadow are barely visible. The soil ramp is only about 3-4 browns with scattered single-pixel dots, and the whole piece uses just 10 colours, against 80 for the grass reference. The soil has none of the clustered, per-clump shading that the grass and paving references show. The result is thinner and flatter than the Beodeul standard, and the described puddle feature is under-delivered. When in doubt, fail.
